title: General Stubblebine's $2 billion offer

tellings.quote: You know what kind of I said, well, in '92, General Stubble offered me $2 billion.
And Stubble is first on the scene to you know ostensibly try to almost recruit him into some sort of government program.
tellings.difference: Told by the host, without the $2 billion figure or the 1992 date.
tellings.link_reason: Stubblebine's attempt to recruit Greer into a government program; it matches Greer's own story of Stubblebine's 1992 offer.

as_told.title: Stubblebine tries to recruit Steven Greer

tellings.quote: I think according to documents and emails on the DPI archive, that $2 billion, which still is an egregious sum of money, was to purchase Steven Greer's institution, Cetti, and integrate it into Stubble's work.
tellings.difference: Says the money was to buy CSETI and fold it into Stubblebine's work, citing the DPI archive.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about General Stubblebine's 1992 offer of $2 billion to Greer.

as_told.title: $2 billion offer to buy Greer's CSETI

plain: A UFO campaigner named Steven Greer says that in 1992 a retired Army general named Albert Stubblebine offered him $2 billion, and Michels describes Stubblebine as first on the scene, seemingly trying to recruit Greer into a government programme. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb adds, citing a collection of documents and emails he calls the DPI archive, that the money was meant to buy Greer's organisation, known as CSETI, and fold it into Stubblebine's own work. Told this way, it suggests insiders wanted to bring Greer's efforts under their control.
